description: brief-22/24 split the mega_eigh_med BACK-TRANSFORM onto batched GEMMs (1.13-1.51x on shapes 2/3/8/12); the fresh profile shows this SHIFTED the bottleneck: the single-CTA mega_eigh_med_split_k's remaining stages 1-3 (Householder TRIDIAGONALIZATION) are now 85.9% of shape 2 (n=352) and large fractions of 3/8/12, dominated by the O(n^3)-SIMT serial per-column symv + rank-2 trailing update running one-CTA-per-matrix (n=352 b40 = 40 CTAs on 148 SMs = latency-bound at ~27% occupancy). Apply the SAME split that won the back-transform: BLOCK the tridiagonalization into panels of NB reflectors (LAPACK sytrd-style -- accumulate the panel's Householder vectors V and W in-kernel, then apply the two-sided trailing update A -= V W^T + W V^T as ONE BATCHED GEMM across ALL matrices at the torch level, saturating the GPU where the single-CTA kernel cannot). Keep the Sturm eigenvalues + twisted eigenvectors + already-split batched-GEMM back-transform. DISTINCT from the refuted large-dense-reduction briefs 1/3/4: those competed vs cuSOLVER filling the GPU with 640 matrices at n=512; here the competitor is OUR OWN low-occupancy single-CTA kernel at n=352 b40 and the k=352-384 inner blocks -- exactly the regime where brief-22 PROVED the batched-GEMM split wins (1.51x). FP32 for the trailing GEMM (brief-22 measured tf32x3 Ozaki tax > tensor-core gain at n<=512; plain TF32 breaks orth). Route via existing med/inner-solve paths; per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback; -O3/--use_fast_math (accepted-best flags, NOT -O2); no 'stream' substring; forks best 391107f7. Compounds across shapes 2/3/8/12.

BUILT + MEASURED the blocked (LAPACK sytrd/latrd) tridiagonalization with the O(n^3) two-sided TRAILING UPDATE A-=VW^T+WV^T split out to a batched FP32 GEMM at the torch level (mega_latrd_panel_k does panel reflector-gen + BLAS-2 symv against the FIXED panel-start A0; torch does the trailing syr2k; mega_post_tridiag_k does Sturm+twisted+block-T; existing batched-GEMM WY back-transform kept). Correct: numerically equivalent to per-column (V truly tridiagonalizes A0 to 1e-7), validated 39/39 TWICE under -O3/--use_fast_math, eigr 2.3e-6, 0 fallback.

BEST (t9, 9316a7a0): batch-gated geomean 36331us vs parent 36398 (-0.2%, within noise). shape12 (b60, n=1024 geom, k=384 inner) blocked 33468 vs parent 33965 = -1.5% CONSISTENT (t7 33531, t9 33468). shapes 2/3/8 recovered to single-launch (no regression).

KEY MEASURED FINDING -- the blocked-GEMM split's win is BATCH-WINDOWED, not universal (it does NOT compound across 2/3/8/12 as hypothesized):
- b40 (shape2 n=352 DIRECT): blocked 9171 vs single-launch 6774 -> LOSE (35%). At b40 BOTH the panel symv (40 CTAs) AND the trailing GEMM (40 matrices) are under-parallelized; blocking just adds 11 launches+reloads. The single-launch (whole tridiag in ONE launch, A resident in SMEM once) is unbeatable here.
- b640 (shape3 k=352, shape8 k=384 INNER): blocked 94904/93720 vs single-launch 81042/93320 -> LOSE (shape3 +17%). At b640 the single-CTA kernel ALREADY fills 148 SMs with 640 CTAs, so there is NO occupancy headroom for the batched GEMM to exploit; blocking is pure overhead.
- b60 (shape12 INNER k=384): the ONLY win (-1.5%), where B=60<148 (single-CTA SM-starved) AND the trailing GEMM gets enough matrices to amortize the launches.
So gated _latrd_use to 48<=b<=128; b40/b640 keep mega_eigh_med_split.

WHY DISTINCT FROM brief-22's 1.51x back-transform split (which DID win at b40): the back-transform runs the kernel ONCE then does the GEMMs separately. The tridiag REQUIRES interleaving (each panel needs the prior trailing update), forcing 11 kernel launches + 11 A0 reloads (Sigma ns^2 ~ n^3/3 extra global traffic) + 11 trailing GEMMs; that interleave overhead exceeds the BLAS-3 gain at the benchmark batch sizes.

TRIAL ARC: t1 41740 (+14.7%, panel-kernel had O(nb^2) serial per-e block-reductions in the latrd correction); t2 40811 (SMEM Vp/Wp + parallel warp-per-e correction, shape2 40825->30318); t3 38905 (FP32 global symv + FOUND+FIXED the wstride bug: last panel kpan<nbt mis-indexed Wout -> garbage trailing update -> 100% fallback -> eigr 7.6e-2->2.3e-6); t4 37234 (FP16-SMEM packed-A0 symv, accurate now that wstride fixed, shape2 15962->9162); t5 37667 (wired inner solve, revealed b640 regression); t6 37680 (scratch cache, no change -> latency not alloc); t7 36321 (batch-gate); t8 36461 (nb=16 worse -> fewer/bigger panels better; nb SMEM-capped=24@k384/32@n352 is best); t9 36331 FINAL.

OPEN DIRECTIONS (surfaced, not closed):
(1) The interleave overhead is the whole cost. A COOPERATIVE-GRID persistent kernel (one launch, cooperative_groups::grid.sync between panels, trailing syr2k done in-kernel cooperatively across ALL CTAs rather than 1-per-matrix) would keep A resident and kill the reloads/relaunches -- could make the blocked win at b40/b640 too. Untried (needs cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel + a cross-CTA syr2k).
(2) Two-stage band reduction (dense->band via batched GEMM, band->tridiag by a cheap bulge-chase) -- the classic way to get the tridiag O(n^3) onto BLAS-3/tensor-cores; the trailing update there is naturally one big GEMM per sweep. Distinct from this single-stage latrd.
(3) shape12's bottleneck is now the low-rank CQR2 (batch_trsm_left 19.9% + potrf + cutlass GEMMs), NOT the tridiag (12.7%) -- a separate lever (faster batched CholeskyQR / Newton-Schulz orthonormalization for the k=384 dominant subspace).
(4) shape2 (b40, 85.9% single-CTA tridiag) still wants a parallelism win the single-launch can't give at 40 CTAs -- e.g. 2-CTA-per-matrix cooperative tridiag (like the cluster kernel brief-21) rather than the torch-GEMM split.
(5) The trailing GEMM stayed plain FP32; at b640 (if the cooperative-grid idea removes the reload penalty) tf32x3 on the trailing update could add tensor-core throughput.
